evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Never asked. Rep moved directly from probing logistics into pricing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Not applicable — no concerns were raised because the two-concerns question was never asked.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Not addressed. Rep quoted $190/hour for Tuesday October 27th with a $70 trip fee but made no mention of cheaper days or date flexibility.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Never asked for the business. Rep provided pricing ($640 for three hours plus trip fee) and customer said 'I'm gonna get another quote, it's a little bit pricey,' and rep replied 'No problem... feel free to give us a callback.' No ask, no rate lock, no close.

top_strength: Jules gathered essential logistics details efficiently (move date, origin/destination addresses, property type, floor level, move scope) and stayed calm when the customer declined to provide an email.
coaching_note: The two-concerns question must come early in step 2 before any probing starts — it frames the entire conversation and gives the customer a chance to surface what actually matters to them. Without it, you miss the chance to address their real fears and build trust before pricing.
